record.paper_title: On Plane Geometric Spanners: A Survey and Open Problems
record.original_question: Determine the best possible upper bound on the worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation of a planar point set. In addition, decide whether one can prove a strictly smaller worst-case upper bound when the input points are in convex position.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2. What is the best upper bound on the spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation? Can one prove a smaller upper bound on the spanning ratio for points in convex position?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the Euclidean plane in general position (no four points cocircular). The Delaunay triangulation $\mathrm{DT}(P)$ is the planar straight-line graph on vertex set $P$ in which three points $p,q,r \in P$ form a triangular face if and only if the open disk circumscribing $p,q,r$ contains no other point of $P$. For two points $u,v \in P$, let $d_{\mathrm{DT}(P)}(u,v)$ denote the length of a shortest path from $u$ to $v$ in $\mathrm{DT}(P)$, where each edge is weighted by its Euclidean length, and let $\|u-v\|$ denote the Euclidean distance. The (worst-case) spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation is
$$\rho \;=\; \sup_{P}\;\max_{u\neq v\in P}\;\frac{d_{\mathrm{DT}(P)}(u,v)}{\|u-v\|},$$
where the supremum is over all finite planar point sets $P$ in general position.

(a) Determine the exact value of $\rho$, or prove the best possible upper and lower bounds on $\rho$.

(b) Let $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}}$ denote the analogous quantity where the supremum is restricted to point sets $P$ in convex position (i.e., the points of $P$ are the vertices of a convex polygon). Prove or disprove that $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}} < \rho$, and determine the best possible upper bound on $\rho_{\mathrm{conv}}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The exact worst-case spanning ratio of the Euclidean Delaunay triangulation remains open. The best known upper bound is approximately 1.998 (Xia, 2013), improving the classical 2.42 bound of Keil–Gutwin (1989); the best known lower bound is approximately 1.5846 (disproving the long-standing π/2 conjecture). For points in convex position, the previously known bound 2.33 (Cui–Kanj–Xia, 2009) has been superseded by the general 1.998 bound, and no strictly smaller upper bound specifically for convex position has been established.

status_evidence.title: The Stretch Factor of the Delaunay Triangulation Is Less Than 1.998
status_evidence.snippet: The stretch factor of the Delaunay triangulation of a set of points in the plane is less than 1.998, improving the previous best upper bound of 2.42 by Keil and Gutwin (1989).
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound on the Delaunay spanning ratio is 1.998.

status_evidence.title: The Tight Spanning Ratio of the Rectangle Delaunay Triangulation
status_evidence.snippet: Proving a tight bound on the stretch factor of the Delaunay triangulation has been a long standing open problem... known to be between roughly 1.5846 and 1.998.
status_evidence.claim: Determining the exact spanning ratio of the Delaunay triangulation remains open.
